title: Impact of a pre-feeding oral stimulation program on first feed attempt in preterm infants
author: Karine Da Rosa Pereira
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bcp6ivre

steps.title: Randomize neonates into groups
steps.instruction: Use the Random Alloc Software environment to allocate neonates into intervention or control groups using a four-block design.

substeps.instruction: Stratify the sample for randomization into groups: 26-27, 28-29, 30-31, and 32 weeks.
Randomly allocate neonates by stratum into the intervention group (GI) or control group (GII).

steps.title: Implement oral stimulation intervention
steps.instruction: Start the intervention in the 31st week of postmenstrual age, based on clinical stability, for 10 consecutive days.

substeps.instruction: For the Intervention Group (GI): Perform 12 minutes of stroking the cheeks in a circular motion and stroking the vestibular region of the lips, gums, and tongue with fingertips in an anteroposterior direction, followed by 3 minutes of nonnutritive sucking.

For the Control Group (GII): Perform a sham intervention consisting of remaining beside the incubator for the same duration, placing the infant in the proper position, and administering gentle perioral touch without performing oral stimulation maneuvers.

steps.title: Assess oral feeding skills (OFS)
steps.instruction: Perform the OFS assessment once the neonate is clinically stable and at 33 weeks or older of postmenstrual age, regardless of weight.

substeps.instruction: Conduct the assessment during the first attempt at oral feeding as prescribed by the attending physician.
Ensure the assessment is performed by a single speech language pathologist blinded to group allocation.
Use a bottle with a slow flow nipple.
Follow the specific assessment protocol proposed by 'A novel approach to assess oral feeding skills of preterm infants.. Neonatology.'

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze data using PASW Statistics® for Windows, Version 18.0 software.

substeps.instruction: Express categorical variables as absolute and relative frequencies; describe symmetrically distributed continuous variables as means and standard deviations, and asymmetrical distributed categorical variables as medians and interquartile ranges.
Use Fisher’s exact test for categorical variables and Student’s t test for symmetrically distributed quantitative variables.
Use the Mann–Whitney test for asymmetrically distributed variables.
Apply bivariate analysis (p < 0.20) to ascertain involved factors.
Use multiple Poisson regression with robust variance to evaluate independent association of factors in level 4 (L4) status.
Use generalized estimating equations (GEE) to analyze volume intake in the first days of oral feeding during the transition from tube to oral feeding.
Apply Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons.
Use Log rank test for analysis of time until transition to full oral feeding.
Use Cox multivariable regression to control for breastfeeding rates.
